pool.title: Unblock CLI retries; stop false leak alarms
pool.body: Two stalls, both reproduced by running the kit in a scratch copy. First: when a CLI or API agent returns invalid output, ingest writes a retry prompt and prints `RUN council.py dispatch`, but cmd_dispatch skips any agent whose output file exists, so it answers `nothing to dispatch` and ingest rejects the same file again. Every cross-lab elder travels this path. Fix: move the rejected file aside when the retry prompt is written, and name the agents in the printed retry line. Second: the identity-leak check flags ordinary cost phrases built on the word for a council place (five of five tried), forcing rewrites at merge. Narrow it to real ids. One unit test for each.
pool.eli5: Two stuck buttons: a retry that does nothing, and a blind-check alarm that rings at ordinary words.

pool.title: Next resumes: spawn only missing seats
pool.body: After a context reset the chair runs status, then next. Today next rewrites every prompt and prints SPAWN lines for all seats of the phase, including seats whose valid output is already on disk, so a reset mid-fan-out re-spawns up to seven agents at roughly 60k tokens each and overwrites good work. Fix: next validates existing outputs first and prints only the seats still missing or invalid, with a line such as `5 of 7 in`. It stores an attempt count per agent and prints the exact --force command at the second failure, so the `fails twice` rule no longer lives in chair memory. Status shows the same pending list.
pool.eli5: After a restart, only redo the seats that have not answered, and let the tool count failures.

pool.title: Derive card authors from provenance, not chair input
pool.body: Self-vote exclusion in tally() trusts each card's authors list, and the chair types that list by hand twice: in pool.json at merge and in candidates.json at fuse. _check_cards only checks that authors is a non-empty list of expert ids; nothing reads the from or parents fields. A fused card built from two experts' cards but labelled with a third expert's id lets those two rank their own work, unrecorded. Fix: ingest_merge requires every from ref to be a real kept-card ref and sets authors to those experts; ingest_fuse requires parents to be shortlisted pool ids and sets authors to the union of the parents' authors. One unit test covers both.
pool.eli5: The computer, not the referee, writes whose idea each card came from, so nobody can vote for their own.

pool.title: Give each voter its own candidate order
pool.body: blind() is seeded only by run, loop and phase, so every voter in a phase gets the identical packet, and the same card sits first on all seven ballots. LLM judges show measurable position bias (Zheng et al. 2023, MT-Bench), so a shared order adds the same tilt to every ballot and Borda sums it instead of cancelling it. Fix: keep one label-to-card mapping per phase, but have write_seat_prompts render each seat's copy in a rotated order (Latin square over seats), so each card leads about equally often. Labels, mapping and tally are unchanged; no model calls. Test: with seats at least equal to cards, every label leads some packet.
pool.eli5: Everyone sees the cards in a different order, so being listed first stops giving a free boost.

pool.title: Reject agents only for faults the run reads
pool.body: Every rejected expert is a full respawn: about 60k tokens of host overhead plus the whole task again, and after two failures the chair must drop that voice, breaking the seven-lens rule. Three checks guard nothing downstream: ideas over 25 words (only counted; check_run already treats them as a warning), incomplete elder scores (stored, never read by cut or final), and ballots missing, repeating or misnaming a label (tally already ranks gaps neutrally). Make the first two warnings, repair ballots missing up to one in ten labels, and log each repair in run.json. Self-vote exclusion and blind labels stay untouched. Idea count, card shape and verdicts stay hard errors.
pool.eli5: Do not make an expert redo everything because one idea line ran long or a ballot skipped one name.
